fi-ctenopoma-acutirostre.title: Leopard Ctenopoma
fi-ctenopoma-acutirostre.summary: The leopard bushfish, Ctenopoma acutirostre, is an anabantoid from the middle Congo River basin, from Malebo Pool upstream to Boyoma Falls. Often sold as 'spotted climbing perch', it mimics leaves…
rows: Carnivore / micropredator. An obligate predator which probably feeds on smaller fishes and invertebrates in nature, but in most cases adapts well to dead alternatives in captivity.
Widely distributed throughout the middle Congo River basin in Republic of the Congo, Democratic Republic of the Congo, and Central African Republic, from Malebo (Stanley) Pool…
notes: Prefers a dimly-lit aquarium with a layer of surface vegetation, such as Ceratopteris spp., plus some submerged cover.
Driftwood roots and branches plus plant species such as Anubias can be used to achieve the latter, while the addition of dried leaf litter is also recommended.

fi-erpetoichthys-calabaricus.title: Ropefish
fi-erpetoichthys-calabaricus.summary: The ropefish, Erpetoichthys calabaricus, is a nocturnal polypterid from shallow, heavily vegetated waters in Western Africa. The only member of its genus, it is closely related to Polypterus, and its…
rows: Widespread in Western Africa, it's been collected in Democratic Republic of Congo, Angola, Nigeria, Cameroon, Equatorial Guinea, Benin.
notes: A densely planted aquarium with a soft substrate and pieces of driftwood forming hiding places is ideal for this fish.
A tight-fitting cover is essential as this fish is an excellent escape artist.

fi-hydrocynus-vittatus.title: African Vittatus Tiger Fish
fi-hydrocynus-vittatus.summary: The African tiger fish, Hydrocynus vittatus, is a large predatory alestid found throughout Africa, from Egypt to South Africa. A voracious piscivore with dagger-shaped, interlocking teeth, it hunts…
rows: Usually kept singly (or a known pair when breeding)
Predator / carnivore. It is a piscivore by nature and many sources state that it will only feed on live fish.
Widespread throughout Africa, from Egypt to South Africa.
notes: There is no need for any decor except perhaps a sandy base due to the speed and power of these fish.
Water should be of the highest quality and well-oxygenated.

fi-pantodon-buchholzi.title: African Butterfly
fi-pantodon-buchholzi.summary: The African butterfly fish, Pantodon buchholzi, is a surface-dwelling osteoglossiform from still and slow waters in West and Central Africa. The only member of its genus and family, it takes its name…
rows: It is mainly an insectivore in nature and a varied diet of live and frozen foods such as bloodworm, brine shrimp, prawn, small mealworms etc.
Republic of Congo, Democratic Republic of Congo, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Benin, Chad, Nigeria, Sierra Leone, Niger, Gabon.
notes: This species does best in slightly soft, acidic water, preferably stained with tannins.
Any water movement should be kept to a minimum.

fi-periophthalmus-barbarus.title: African Mudskipper
fi-periophthalmus-barbarus.summary: The Atlantic mudskipper, Periophthalmus barbarus, is a highly amphibious goby from the west African coast, from Mauritania south to Angola. It lives on and around mudflats in estuarine mangrove…
rows: group of 5 or more can be kept.
Feeds chiefly on crabs, insects and other invertebrates in the wild but is surprisingly adaptable in captivity.
This species occurs throughout most of the west African coastline, from Mauritania in the north southwards as far as Angola.
notes: A bank or beach made of sand or mudflat mud is suggested but you could use partially submerged bogwood.
